texts.preamble: Kamal Kumar Arora vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 6 December, 2017 The High Court Of Madhya Pradesh Mcrc-17820-2017 (Kamal Kumar Arora Vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh) 5 Jabalpur, Dated : 06-12-2017
texts.arguments: The contention of the petitioner is that the provision of Section 13(2) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 has not been complied with and also that the criminal complaint is pending since last 17 years without having examined any of the prosecution witness. The categoric stand of the petitioner is that there was a violation of mandatory requirement in terms of Section 13(2) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, inasmuch as that the petitioner was never given option for re-testing of the second sample before the Central Laboratory at Mysore. The contention of learned counsel for the petitioner for the first time was noticed in the order dated 06.12.2017 and following order was passed. "The contention of the petitioner is that the provision of Section 13(2) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 has not been complied with and also that the criminal complaint is pending since last 17 years without having examined any of the prosecution witness. Learned Government Advocate for the respondent-State is directed to seek instructions as to whether compliance has been made or not?
texts.petitioner_arguments: The contention of the petitioner is that the provision of Section 13(2) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 has not been complied with and also that the criminal complaint is pending since last 17 years without having examined any of the prosecution witness.
